L: The flight to San Antonio leaves at fourteen fifteen, not at four fifteen.
items.e: In military time, fourteen fifteen (1415) is 2:15 p.m. The speaker corrects the mistake "four fifteen".

L: Would you mind closing the window?
o: Not at all. I'll do it now.
At the end of the hall.
items.e: "Would you mind...?" is a polite request. "Not at all" means "I don't mind": the speaker agrees to help.

L: Are you driving to Dallas this weekend?
I was going to, but my car is in the shop, so I'll take the bus.
items.q: How will the man travel to Dallas?
items.e: "I was going to (drive), but my car is in the shop" (being repaired), "so I'll take the bus".

L: The jacket was eighty dollars, but I got it for half price.
items.q: How much did the woman pay?
items.e: Half of eighty dollars is forty dollars.

L: Private Kim arrived after the formation had already started.
o: Private Kim was late for the formation.
Private Kim was early for the formation.
items.e: Past perfect: the formation had started before he arrived, so he was late.

L: The bus to the airport leaves every twenty minutes. The next one is at ten forty.
items.q: When does the bus after the 10:40 bus leave?
items.e: 10:40 plus 20 minutes is 11:00.

L: Do you want to eat at the dining facility or go off base?
Let's stay here. It's raining too hard to drive.
items.e: "Let's stay here": they will not drive off base, so they will eat at the dining facility on base.

L: I'd have called you if I had known you were in town.
o: He did not know the listener was in town.
He knew the listener was in town.
He will call the listener later.
items.e: Third conditional: an unreal past. He did not know, so he did not call.

L: Have you ever been to New York?
o: Yes, I went there two years ago.
Yes, I'm going there next week.
items.e: "Have you ever...?" asks about past experience. Only "Yes, I went there two years ago" talks about a past visit.

L: Can you cover my shift on Saturday?
Sorry, my hands are tied. I'm on duty all weekend.
items.e: "My hands are tied" means "I am not free to do it": she cannot help.

L: The hotel costs a hundred and twenty dollars a night, but the travel office will only pay ninety.
So I'll have to pay the difference myself.
items.q: How much will the man pay for each night?
items.e: The hotel costs "a hundred and twenty dollars a night", and the travel office pays "ninety". The man pays the difference, $120 - $90 = $30.

L: So the cargo plane lands at zero seven hundred, and we finish unloading by noon?
Exactly. I'm glad we're on the same page.
o: They are reading the same report.
The plane will land at noon.
The plan is still not clear.
items.e: "We're on the same page" means "We understand the plan in the same way." She agrees with what the man said.

L: It's almost five o'clock. Can you still send me the delivery schedule today?
Sorry, I can't. I'll send it first thing in the morning.
items.q: When will the woman send the schedule?
items.e: "First thing in the morning" means early the next morning, before anything else. She "can't" send it today.

L: You look pale. Are you all right?
I'm a little under the weather, that's all.
o: He got wet in the rain.
He does not like the weather.
items.e: "Under the weather" means a little sick. It has nothing to do with rain or the weather outside.

L: The neighbors had another loud party last night. It went on until two in the morning.
That's the last straw. I'm going to talk to the building manager today.
o: He will not accept the noise any longer.
He thinks it was the last party.
He wants to join the next party.
He spoke to the manager last night.
items.e: "That's the last straw" means "I can't accept this any more." After "another loud party", he is going to complain to the building manager.

L: Can I take the van to the training area this afternoon?
Not unless you want to push it. The battery's dead.
o: The van cannot be driven right now.
The man should push the van there.
The van needs more fuel first.
She will drive the man there herself.
items.e: "Not unless you want to push it" is a joke that means no. The van will not start because "the battery's dead".

L: We're getting pizza tonight. Do you want to come?
I'd love to, but I really need to hit the books.
o: He has to return some books.
items.e: "Hit the books" means study hard. He would like to go, but he has to study.

L: Are you going to apply for the instructor course in Texas?
I already did, but it's a long shot.
o: She does not expect to be accepted.
The course lasts a very long time.
Texas is very far from here.
She has not sent her application yet.
items.e: "A long shot" is something with little chance of success. She has applied, but she does not think she will be accepted.

L: Where were you? We waited for you for half an hour.
Sorry. I was reading in the library and lost track of time.
o: She did not notice how late it was.
She lost her watch in the library.
She got lost on the way.
She could not find her book.
items.e: To "lose track of time" means to stop noticing the time. She was busy reading and did not see how late it was.

L: Dinner was great. Let me get the check this time.
That's nice of you, but let's go Dutch tonight.
o: They should each pay for their own meal.
The man should pay for both meals.
They should eat at a Dutch restaurant.
She should pay for both meals.
items.e: "Let's go Dutch" means that each person pays for his or her own meal. She thanks him but does not let him pay for both.

L: We're having a barbecue on Sunday. Can you and your husband come?
I'd love to, but can I take a rain check? My parents are visiting this weekend.
o: She would like to come another time instead.
She will come if it does not rain.
She will bring her parents to the barbecue.
She needs to check the weather first.
items.e: "Can I take a rain check?" is a polite way to say "I can't come this time, but please ask me again." It has nothing to do with rain.

L: If I borrow ten thousand dollars for a car, how much will I pay each month?
I'd need to check a few details, but a ballpark figure would be three hundred dollars a month.
o: The monthly payment of $300 is only an estimate.
The monthly payment will be exactly $300.
The bank will lend him only $300.
items.e: A "ballpark figure" is a rough number. She still needs to "check a few details", so $300 is only an estimate.

L: The barracks inspection got moved up to Wednesday.
Wednesday? I was counting on the weekend to get my wall locker squared away.
o: She has less time to prepare than planned.
She will be away on the day of the inspection.
She doesn't know where her wall locker is.
She thought the inspection had been canceled.
items.e: "Moved up" means earlier, so she loses the weekend she had planned to use to prepare.

L: Are you ready for the inspection?
As ready as I'll ever be.
o: She has done all she can to prepare.
She is not ready at all.
items.e: The expression means she has prepared as much as possible.

L: I've got a sick call appointment at zero seven thirty, but formation's at the same time.
Medical comes first. Just let your squad leader know before you head over.
items.q: What does the woman advise the man to do?
o: Inform his supervisor and go to the clinic.
Attend formation and reschedule the visit.
Ask his squad leader to go with him.
Go to the clinic after formation ends.
items.e: She says the appointment is more important; he only needs to tell his squad leader first.

L: The inspector general's team arrives Tuesday. How do our supply records look?
Honestly, I wouldn't want anyone looking at them before Thursday at the earliest.
o: The records are not ready for the inspection.
The inspection has been pushed back to Thursday.
She will review the records on Tuesday.
The records were checked earlier this week.
items.e: She needs until at least Thursday, but the inspectors come Tuesday, so the records aren't ready.

L: Is it okay if I leave early today?
o: She wants him to visit her.
items.e: "Be my guest" gives permission.

L: Did you hear the news about the base closing?
Yes, it came as a total shock.
items.e: "A total shock" means a big surprise.

L: Did you finish reading the novel?
o: The book was so good she read it without stopping.
items.e: "Couldn't put it down" means very engaging.

L: It was a little too salty for my taste.
o: The soup had too much salt.
items.e: She found it too salty.

L: Is the new dining facility any good?
items.e: "So-so" means neither good nor bad.

L: Do you want to try skydiving with me?
o: She doesn't want to do it.
items.e: "Count me out" means don't include me.

L: Are the trainees ready for the march?
o: They are very eager to start.
items.e: "Raring to go" means very eager.

L: Did you send the training schedule to the battalion yet?
It's ready to go, but the operations officer asked for one more change before it goes out.
items.q: Why hasn't the schedule been sent?
o: It still needs to be revised.
The battalion already has a copy.
Nobody has typed it up yet.
items.e: The operations officer wants another change made before it is sent.

L: Did you see the game last night?
I wouldn't have missed it for anything.
items.e: She considered it too important to miss.

L: Is your sister coming to the wedding?
She wouldn't miss it for the world.
o: Her sister is traveling the world.
items.e: The phrase means she will surely come.

L: Was it hard to find my house?
items.e: "Spot on" means exactly correct.

L: Did you like living in Germany?
I'd go back in a heartbeat.
items.e: "In a heartbeat" means immediately and gladly.

L: The printer is out of paper again.
There's a new box in the supply closet.
items.q: What will the man probably do?
o: Get paper from the supply closet
items.e: She tells him where to find paper.

L: My car won't start this morning.
Let me get the jumper cables from my trunk.
items.q: What will the woman probably do?
items.e: Jumper cables are used to start a car with a dead battery.

L: Your blood pressure is fine, but you need to lose some weight.
items.e: Checking blood pressure is a doctor's job.

L: There's a gas station just ahead; let's stop there.
o: Change the tire on the highway
items.e: She suggests stopping at the gas station ahead.

L: I'd like to sign out a laptop for the staff meeting tomorrow.
I can do that, but it has to be back on my desk by sixteen hundred.
items.q: What does the woman tell the man?
o: He must return it by four in the afternoon.
He can keep it for the whole week.
He has to return it by six o'clock.
He needs to bring it to a meeting at four.
items.e: Sixteen hundred is military time for 4:00 p.m.

L: Let's take a picture in front of the fountain.
Okay, I'll ask someone to take it for us.
items.q: What will the woman probably do?
o: Ask a stranger to take a photo
items.e: She'll ask someone to photograph them.

L: All passengers must fasten their seat belts.
items.e: Seat belt announcements are made on planes.

L: Oops, I left it in the truck. I'll go get it.
o: Get the map from the truck
items.e: He will go back for it.

L: I'm sorry, I'll bring you another bowl.
items.e: Replacing food at a table is a waiter's job.

L: I'd like a large pepperoni pizza for delivery.
Can I have your address, please?
items.e: She orders a pizza for delivery.

L: That's me. I have an appointment at ten.
items.e: Patients and appointments suggest a clinic.

L: Can you recommend a good dish?
items.e: Recommending dishes is a server's job.

L: I'm going to the gym. Want to come?
Sure, just let me get my shoes.
o: Get her shoes and go to the gym
items.e: She agrees to go after getting her shoes.

L: I'd like a haircut and a shave.
Have a seat; I'll be right with you.
items.e: Haircuts and shaves happen at a barber shop.

L: My essay is due tomorrow, and I haven't started.
You'd better get to work right now.
items.e: She advises starting now.

L: My ears pop every time the plane lands.
o: He gets airsick on every flight.
He chews too much gum on planes.
items.e: His ears pop, an uncomfortable feeling, whenever the plane comes down to land.

L: Is the meeting in Room Ten?
No, they moved it to Room Twelve.
items.e: It moved to Room Twelve.

L: I think we should take the highway.
The back roads would be faster at this hour.
items.e: She prefers the back roads.

L: How many people are in your unit?
About three hundred, but a third are deployed.
items.e: A third of three hundred is one hundred.

L: When do we get paid this month?
On the thirtieth, since the first is a Sunday.
items.e: Payday moves to the thirtieth.

L: It left on time but landed an hour late.
items.e: It landed an hour late.

L: Should we leave at six or seven?
Six; traffic gets bad after six thirty.
items.q: Why does the woman want to leave at the earlier time?
o: To beat the rush on the roads
Because the roads close at six thirty
Because she has to be home by seven
To pick someone up at six thirty
items.e: She says traffic gets bad after six thirty, so leaving at six avoids it.

L: Is the new clerk faster than the one who left?
Faster, sure, but I end up fixing half of what she types.
items.q: What does the woman imply about the new clerk?
o: She is slower than the clerk who left.
She types only half of the documents.
She helps the woman correct her work.
items.e: The clerk is quick, but much of her typing has to be corrected.

L: Parts of it were, but it was too long.
items.q: What did the woman think of the lecture?
items.e: She liked parts but found it long.

L: Do you like your new job better than the old one?
The pay is better, but the hours are longer.
items.q: What does the woman say about her new job?
o: It pays more but takes more time.
She doesn't like it at all.
items.e: Better pay, longer hours.

L: How many times have you been to Korea?
items.q: How many times has she been to Korea before?
items.e: "This will be my third" means two previous trips.

L: When do you have to sign in at your new unit?
No later than the first of June, but I'm driving, so I'm leaving a week early.
items.q: When does the woman plan to leave?
o: A week after the first of June.
items.e: She must arrive by June first and is leaving a week before that, around May 25.

L: I think we should cancel the picnic.
Let's wait and see what the weather does.
items.e: "Wait and see" means decide later.

L: I can't believe it's already December.
o: Time passes quickly when you're busy.
items.e: The saying means time seems to pass fast.

L: There's an indoor one and an outdoor one.
o: There is only an indoor pool.
There is only an outdoor pool.
items.e: One indoor and one outdoor.

L: Did the new desks for the office ever arrive?
They came Monday, but they're too wide to fit through the door, so they're sitting in the hallway.
items.q: What is the problem with the desks?
o: They can't be moved inside the room.
They are too small for the office.
They were taken to the wrong building.
items.e: The desks arrived but are too wide for the door, so they can't go into the office.

L: Why didn't you come to the gym this morning?
I pulled a muscle in my back yesterday.
items.q: Why didn't the man go to the gym?
items.e: A pulled muscle kept him away.

L: Why is the line so long?
items.e: One cashier slows the line.

L: I haven't heard from my son in two weeks.
o: He has had no news from his son.
items.e: Two weeks without news worries him.

L: Why are you wearing civilian clothes on a duty day?
I'm out-processing today. My last formation with this unit was yesterday.
items.q: What can be concluded about the man?
o: He is on sick leave today.
He forgot his uniform at home.
items.e: Out-processing and having had his last formation mean he is moving to another assignment.

L: What's the matter with the radio?
There's a lot of static; I can't hear anything.
items.q: What is wrong with the radio?
items.e: Static makes it impossible to hear.

L: Why do you want to change jobs?
I'd like a chance to travel more.
items.q: Why is the man looking for a different job?
o: He wants to see more places.
His job requires too much travel.
items.e: He wants a job that gives him a chance to travel more.

L: Half the staff is out sick.
items.e: Half the staff is sick.

L: Why do you look so pleased?
My daughter got into the college she wanted.
o: His daughter got into her college.
items.e: Good news about his daughter.

L: Why is Corporal Lane so quiet today?
She didn't get the assignment she wanted.
o: She is disappointed about an assignment.
She is angry at the man.
items.e: Missing the assignment upset her.

L: What's the matter with the coffee?
Someone forgot to add the coffee; it's just hot water.
items.q: What is wrong with the coffee?
items.e: No coffee was added.

L: Why is the river so high?
It's been raining for a week.
items.e: A week of rain raised the river.

L: Why are you selling your bicycle?
items.q: Why is the woman selling her bike?
items.e: She's moving overseas.

L: Why is the classroom so cold?
Someone left the windows open all night.
o: The windows were open all night.
items.e: Open windows let in cold air.

L: Why are there so many police cars outside?
There was a robbery at the bank.
items.e: A robbery brought the police.

L: Why don't you just take some aspirin for that headache?
The doctor told me not to mix it with the medicine I'm already on.
items.q: Why won't the woman take aspirin?
o: It could react with another drug she uses.
Her doctor says it won't help headaches.
She has run out of medicine at home.
Her headache has already gone away.
items.e: Her doctor warned her against combining aspirin with her current medicine.

L: Ma'am, may I have Friday off?
Only if Corporal Tate can cover your shift.
o: He can have Friday off if someone covers for him.
Corporal Tate is off on Friday.
items.e: Permission depends on coverage.

L: Is the briefing still at fourteen hundred?
It's been moved to fifteen hundred.
items.e: 1500 hours is 3 p.m.

L: Did you get the new schedule?
It's posted on the bulletin board.
o: She can go look at it herself.
He hasn't seen the new schedule yet.
He will send her a copy by email.
items.e: Since the schedule is posted on the bulletin board, she can go and read it there.

L: Can I use the conference room this afternoon?
It's reserved until three; after that it's free.
items.q: When can the woman use the room?
items.e: It is free after three.

L: Have you heard whether you were selected for the leadership course?
The list comes out Friday, but my first sergeant hinted that I shouldn't make any other plans.
items.q: What does the man's first sergeant suggest?
o: He should plan to take leave.
He was not selected this time.
items.e: Telling him not to make other plans is a hint that he will be selected.

L: The jackets did, but the pants were too long.
items.q: What was the problem with the uniforms?
o: The trousers needed to be shorter.
The jackets were too big for him.
items.e: The jackets fit, but the pants were too long, so they needed shortening.

L: Report it to security and get a temporary pass.
o: Report it and get a temporary pass
items.e: Reporting the loss is the first step.

L: When does the next class start?
In two weeks, on the first of the month.
items.q: What can be inferred from the man's answer?
o: Today is around the middle of the month.
The class started two weeks ago.
It begins on the second of the month.
The class lasts for two weeks.
items.e: If the first of the month is two weeks away, it is now about the middle of the month.

L: There are spares in the commo room.
o: Take an extra one from the commo room
Charge the battery in the commo room
Buy a new radio at the PX
Use the radio in the commo room
items.e: Spares are extra batteries, so she can pick one up in the commo room.

L: Did the trainees enjoy the field trip?
items.q: What can be inferred about the trip?
o: It included a stop to see airplanes.
The trainees did not enjoy it.
They flew to the museum by plane.
The museum was closed that day.
items.e: They visited an aviation museum, which shows aircraft, and they loved it.

L: This map is out of date.
Get a new one from the operations office.
items.e: She suggests a current map.

L: Can I bring my family to the unit picnic?
items.e: Families are invited.

L: How did you get promoted so fast?
I volunteered for every hard job.
items.q: How did the man get promoted fast?
items.e: Volunteering for difficult work.

L: Is the dining facility serving breakfast on Saturday?
Brunch only, from nine to one.
o: Only a late-morning meal is offered.
Breakfast and lunch are served separately.
It is closed all day Saturday.
items.e: "Brunch only" means there is no regular breakfast, just one combined meal from nine to one.

L: How's the weather at the drop zone?
items.q: What is the weather like at the drop zone?
items.e: Clear with light winds.

L: Can we use the gym for the ceremony?
Only if the auditorium isn't available.
o: The auditorium is the first choice.
The gym is the first choice.
items.e: The gym is the backup.

L: This briefing is excellent. Did you put all of these slides together yourself?
Most of them, but Sergeant Ward did the maps, and those took the longest.
o: She had help with part of the work.
Sergeant Ward made all the slides.
The maps were the easiest part.
items.e: She made most of the slides, but Sergeant Ward made the maps.

L: Her train gets in at six forty.
items.e: Her train gets in.

L: We should throw her a surprise party.
items.q: What does the woman want to do?
o: Secretly plan a celebration for her
items.e: Throwing a surprise party means planning a celebration that the grandmother doesn't know about.

L: How do you like the new neighbors?
They're friendly, but their dog barks a lot.
items.q: What is the problem with the neighbors?
items.e: The barking dog is the issue.

L: Clean and comfortable, but breakfast wasn't included.
items.q: What was missing at the hotel?
items.e: Breakfast wasn't included.

L: Where can I find the batteries?
Aisle seven, next to the flashlights.
o: Beside the flashlights, in the seventh aisle
In aisle eleven, close to the flashlights
In aisle seven, behind the light bulbs
At the front counter, next to the flashlights
items.e: She says aisle seven, next to the flashlights.

L: The bread is a little stale.
items.e: Toast uses stale bread well.

L: Let's go to the later show.
items.e: He suggests the later show.

L: I want to buy a bike for my daughter.
How old is she? We have different sizes.
items.q: Why does the man ask about the daughter's age?
o: To find the right bike size
To check if she can ride
items.e: Bike size depends on age.

L: My mother is coming to stay for a month.
Then we'll need to clean the guest room.
o: The extra room needs tidying first.
Her mother can't stay that long.
They have no room for her mother.
items.e: He says they will need to clean the guest room, so it isn't ready for a guest yet.

L: How do you keep your kitchen so clean?
items.e: Cleaning as he goes keeps it clean.

L: How much is a coffee and a bagel?
items.q: How much does she have to pay?
items.e: The total is $4.25.

L: We have a smaller one on sale.
o: A discount on the expensive TV
items.e: A smaller TV on sale.

L: How long have you lived in this town?
All my life, except for four years in college.
items.q: Where did the man spend four years?
items.e: Four years at college.

L: Should we paint the room white or yellow?
Yellow will make it look warmer.
items.q: Which color does the woman prefer?
items.e: She prefers yellow.

L: At the hospital, as a nurse.
items.q: What is the woman's brother's job?
items.e: He works as a nurse.

L: How much does a ticket to the game cost?
items.e: "How much" asks for a price.

L: How far is the PX from here?
items.e: "How far" asks for distance.

L: Who was the first person to arrive this morning?
items.e: "Who" asks for a person.

L: How much time do we have before the test?
items.e: "How much time" asks for minutes or hours.

L: Do I need to wear my dress uniform to the change of command ceremony?
o: No, the duty uniform is fine.
I wore it to my cousin's wedding.
The command changes every two years.
It was a very long ceremony.
items.e: The reply says the dress uniform is not required; the everyday uniform is acceptable.

L: How late is the armory open if I need to turn in my weapon tonight?
o: The clerk stays there until nine tonight.
I turned mine in this morning.
It's two buildings past the gym.
You were late for formation again.
items.e: If the clerk stays until nine, the armory is open until nine.

L: Why is everyone standing outside? I thought formation was canceled because of the rain.
o: The first sergeant changed his mind.
It rained hard all night up north.
Formation was at six thirty yesterday.
items.e: The first sergeant decided to hold formation after all, so everyone is outside.

L: Why are all the flags at half-staff today?
items.e: "Why" asks for a reason.

L: When will the new barracks be ready?
o: By the end of the year.
items.e: "When" asks for a time.

L: What time is it in Tokyo now?
items.e: "What time" asks for the current hour.

L: Who do I give this form to?
o: Give it to the clerk at the front desk.
items.e: "Who" asks for a person.

L: Where can I get my uniform patches sewn on around here?
o: Try the tailor shop next to the PX.
I sewed mine on last night.
They cost around ten dollars each.
My old uniform doesn't fit anymore.
items.e: A tailor at the post exchange is a place that sews on patches.

L: How long ago did you move here?
items.e: "How long ago" asks for time in the past.

L: How many eggs do you need for the cake?
items.e: "How many" asks for a number.

L: Who left the lights on in the classroom?
o: I think the last class did.
items.e: "Who" asks for a person.

L: Would you mind turning down the radio?
o: Sorry, I'll turn it down now.
items.e: "Would you mind" is a polite request; the reply agrees to do it.

L: How about going for a run after work?
items.e: "How about" is a suggestion.

L: Do you think my boots are shiny enough to pass the inspection tomorrow?
o: Maybe one more coat of polish.
I passed him on my way over here.
They're the boots I wore yesterday.
The inspection was over by ten.
items.e: She suggests the boots are not quite shiny enough yet and need more polish.

L: Can you pick up some bread on your way home?
items.e: The reply agrees and asks for details.

L: I'm going to the snack bar. Can I get you anything?
items.e: It is an offer; the reply makes a request.

L: Would you like to leave a message?
o: Yes, please ask him to call me back.
I left it on the desk.
items.e: It's an offer on the phone.

L: Could you speak a little more slowly, please?
items.e: The reply agrees to the request.

L: Would you like to try on a larger size?
o: Yes, please. This one is too tight.
items.e: A shop offer; the reply accepts with a reason.

L: Shall I make a reservation for four people?
items.e: The reply accepts and adds details.

L: Do you want me to wake you up at six?
o: Yes, please. I have an early meeting.
items.e: The reply accepts the offer.

L: Could you check the tire pressure for me?
o: Sure, let me get the gauge.
items.e: The reply agrees to help.

L: Would you like to come in for a cup of tea?
o: Thanks, but I really have to go.
items.e: The reply declines politely.

L: Would you like me to show you around the base?
items.e: "Show you around" means give a tour.

L: Do the cooks have to go through the weapons refresher training too, or just the infantry?
o: Everyone has to, whatever their job.
The cook's been through a lot lately.
A cold drink would be refreshing.
Just the two of us went.
items.e: "Everyone, whatever their job" means the cooks must take the training too.

L: Is it okay if I pay by credit card?
o: Of course. We take all major cards.
items.e: The reply gives permission.

L: Let me buy you lunch to say thanks.
o: That's not necessary, but thank you.
items.e: The reply politely refuses the offer.

L: Pardon me, could you move your car? It's blocking my driveway.
o: Oh, I'm sorry. I'll move it right away.
items.e: The reply apologizes and agrees.

L: Isn't it a little cold to go swimming?
o: Not for me; I like cold water.
The swimming pool is very large and deep.
I went swimming at the beach last summer.
The water in the pool is changed every week.
items.e: The negative question expects disagreement or agreement; here he disagrees.

L: The test was harder than you expected, wasn't it?
o: The test had fifty questions and two parts.
I expected to take the test on Monday.
We took the test in the language lab.
items.e: The tag question asks for agreement.

L: Where did you get that new reflective belt? Mine is falling apart.
o: Supply had a whole box of them.
It fell off the top shelf yesterday.
Mine is the one on the left.
items.e: He got the belt from the supply room, which had plenty of them.

L: Has anyone told you why the armory is doing a hundred percent inventory this week?
o: Some records didn't match, I heard.
I told her about it on Monday.
About a hundred, more or less.
I'm doing just fine, thanks for asking.
items.e: Records that did not match explain why every item must be counted.

L: You're not going to the range in those sneakers, are you?
o: No, I'll change into boots first.
I bought them on sale last week.
Yes, I've been there twice already.
The range was closed all day yesterday.
items.e: She will put on boots before she goes, so she won't wear the sneakers.

L: Who's supposed to set up the projector for the commander's update tomorrow?
o: Sergeant Ward said he'd take care of it.
The commander got here at nine.
I'm supposed to be off tomorrow.
The project is due next week.
items.e: Sergeant Ward agreed to set up the projector.

L: If I don't pass the CPR certification on the first try, can I retake it?
o: Yes, but you'll have to wait a week.
I passed mine on the first try.
I'll try to take it with me.
items.e: He can take the test again, but only after waiting a week.

L: Why did Private Allen get extra duty after the room inspection this morning?
o: His locker was a complete mess.
There's extra room in the back.
I inspected it myself last week.
items.e: A messy locker explains why Allen was given extra duty.

L: Can you raise headquarters on the radio and tell them we'll be thirty minutes late?
o: I'll try, but the signal's weak here.
They raised my rent again last month.
The headquarters building is brand new.
items.e: "Raise" here means contact by radio; she agrees to try even though the signal is weak.

L: Is the meeting still on for tomorrow?
o: The meeting room is very small.
items.e: "As far as I know" means yes, probably.

L: How many soldiers from our company made it through the air assault course?
o: Only three of the ten who started.
We made it home around midnight.
The air is really dry today.
Our company has about a hundred people.
items.e: Only three soldiers finished the course.

L: Is your new boss easy to work with?
o: My new boss started on Monday.
My boss works in the next office.
items.e: The answer gives an opinion.

L: Is it all right to wear jeans to the party?
items.e: The answer gives permission.

L: Is there a gas station on the way?
o: There's one just before the highway.
My car uses a lot of gas.
items.e: The answer gives the location.

L: Do you think they'll cancel the run if this rain keeps up?
o: Only if there's lightning, I'd guess.
I can't keep up with you.
It rained all last week, and the week before.
items.e: The reply gives an opinion: the run will be canceled only if there is lightning.

L: Is it too late to sign up for the course?
items.e: The answer gives the deadline.

L: How long is this snowstorm supposed to last, do you know?
o: Into tomorrow night, from what I've heard.
I'm supposed to shovel the sidewalks before work.
It was the last one of the season.
items.e: The reply tells how long the storm will continue.

L: When is the deadline for the training report?
o: The training report is ten pages long.
Send the report to the operations office.
items.e: "When" asks for a time.

L: Do you know if the orderly room is still open, or did they close at four?
o: I just saw the clerk locking the door.
Yes, I opened a new account at four.
It's the room at the end of the hall.
The room was very orderly and clean.
items.e: If the clerk was locking the door, the orderly room has already closed.

L: Why did the colonel call a meeting?
o: To talk about the new deployment schedule.
The meeting is in her office.
The colonel calls meetings every week.
items.e: "Why" asks for a reason.

L: Why are you wearing your dress uniform?
o: I have a promotion ceremony this afternoon.
items.e: "Why" asks for a reason.

L: How far is the training area from the main post?
o: The training area is very large.
It takes thirty minutes by truck.
items.e: "How far" asks for distance.

L: Where do we meet for the road march?
o: At the north end of the parade field.
The road march is twelve miles.
The road march starts at five.
items.e: "Where" asks for a place.

L: Where should we store the extra tents?
o: In the warehouse, behind the trucks.
We used the tents last month.
items.e: "Where" asks for a place.

L: Would you rather take the van or the pickup to get supplies in town?
o: Whichever has more gas in it.
I picked up the supplies yesterday.
Yes, I'd rather stay in town.
They're having a sale in town today.
items.e: The speaker has no preference and will take the vehicle with more fuel.

L: Who's in charge while the captain is away?
o: The captain will be away for a week.
The captain is a good leader.
items.e: "Who" asks for a person.

L: How soon will the results be ready?
o: The results are in the office.
items.e: "How soon" asks for time.

L: Wasn't the range supposed to be closed all week for repairs?
o: The stove in my kitchen needs repairs.
It was closer than I thought.
Yes, I paid for the repairs myself.
items.e: The range is open again because the repairs were completed ahead of schedule.

L: How many people can the bus carry?
o: The bus is blue and white.
The bus goes to the airport.
items.e: "How many" asks for a number.

L: How much weight do we carry on the march?
o: The march is twelve miles long.
items.e: "How much weight" asks for an amount.

L: I can't find the form for reenlistment anywhere. Has it been replaced by a new one?
o: Yes, it's all done online now.
I found my keys under the desk.
I reenlisted for four more years.
We replaced the printer last month.
items.e: The paper form is no longer used because the process is now online.

L: Which is cheaper, the bus or the train?
o: The bus, but it takes longer.
I take the bus every day.
items.e: "Which" asks for a comparison.

L: It's a beautiful day. Do you want to eat our lunch outside for a change?
o: Good idea, before it gets too hot.
I don't have any change, sorry.
The lunch menu changes every Monday.
items.e: The speaker agrees to eat outside and suggests going soon.

L: Do you know why they moved the weigh-in from Friday to Monday morning?
o: The scales are being repaired this week.
I weigh about the same as last year.
They moved here on a Friday.
Monday morning is fine with me.
items.e: The weigh-in was moved because the scales cannot be used this week.

L: What kind of car do you drive?
o: I drive to work every day.
My car is in the garage.
items.e: "What kind" asks for a type.

L: What are you doing for the holidays?
o: We're visiting my in-laws in Chicago.
items.e: The question asks for plans.

L: Somebody left the headlights on in the white truck. Is it yours?
o: Mine's the blue one next to it.
I left it on the whiteboard.
The lights are on in the hall.
I'm leaving in the truck at noon.
items.e: The speaker drives a different truck, so the white one isn't his or hers.

L: What's the weather like in Seattle in winter?
items.e: The question asks for a description.

L: How hot is it supposed to get this afternoon? I have outdoor training.
o: I'm supposed to go this afternoon.
It got really hot in the car.
items.e: The reply gives the expected high temperature.

L: You've been sneezing all morning. Is it a cold or just allergies?
o: Pollen gets to me every fall.
It was really cold all morning, wasn't it?
items.e: Pollen causes allergies, so the sneezing is not from a cold.

L: Which color do you prefer, blue or green?
items.e: "Which" asks for a choice.

L: Do you remember if the change of command ceremony is at ten or eleven?
o: Neither; it was moved to one o'clock.
I remember the old commander well.
items.e: The ceremony is at neither time because it was rescheduled.

L: Are you sure this old truck will make it over the mountain pass?
o: As long as we take it slow, we'll be fine.
I passed the test the first time.
The mountain is about six thousand feet high.
I made it myself last summer.
items.e: The speaker believes the truck can do it if they drive slowly.

L: How do you say "thank you" in Spanish?
items.e: The question asks for a translation.

L: What do you do in your free time?
o: I like to read and go fishing.
I have free time on weekends.
I work from nine to five.
items.e: The question asks for activities.

L: How come your sister didn't fly in for the reunion after all?
o: She couldn't get time off from the hospital.
She flew in on a small plane.
The reunion was at my uncle's farm.
After all these years, she still looks the same.
items.e: "How come" asks for a reason, and not getting time off from work explains why the sister stayed away.

L: Hello, I'm returning a call from this number. Did somebody here try to reach me?
o: That may have been my roommate. Hold on.
I'll be back in the office at three.
Yes, I can reach the top shelf.
The number is on the back of the card.
items.e: The speaker offers a likely person who called and asks the caller to wait while checking.

L: Who should I talk to about the leaky faucet in my quarters?
o: It only leaks when it rains.
Yes, it's a very nice place to live.
items.e: The question asks who handles the repair, and the housing maintenance desk is the right place to report it.

L: Would it be all right if I recorded your lecture so I can listen again later?
o: Sure, as long as you don't post it online.
I'll listen to the recording again tomorrow.
The record was set last year.
It was a long lecture, wasn't it?
items.e: The instructor gives permission with one condition.

L: Which unit are we supposed to review for tomorrow's vocabulary quiz?
o: Just the last two we covered.
My unit is stationed at Fort Bliss.
It's short, only about twenty words.
I reviewed it with my teacher.
items.e: The question asks which part of the book to study, and the reply names the last two units.

L: Why don't you wait until payday to buy those new running shoes?
o: These are only on sale until Sunday.
Payday is on the first and the fifteenth.
I wait for the bus every morning.
They run a little small, I think.
items.e: The reply explains why waiting is a bad idea: the sale ends before payday.

L: How did your presentation go in front of the whole class?
o: I was nervous, but it went smoothly.
The whole class went to lunch together.
I presented my ID at the gate.
It's in front of the library.
items.e: "It went smoothly" means the presentation went well.

L: Sorry, I can barely hear you. Are you somewhere with bad reception?
o: I'm in an elevator. Let me call you back.
I heard about it on the radio this morning.
I hear you're moving to Texas.
items.e: Phones get poor reception in elevators, so the speaker offers to call again.

L: Would you like some more of the stew before I put it away?
o: Just a little, thanks. It's delicious.
I put my winter clothes away last week.
items.e: The person accepts a small second serving and compliments the stew.

L: I thought you were going to mow the lawn this afternoon. What happened?
o: The mower wouldn't start, so I gave up.
It happened a long time ago.
He's going to the mall later this afternoon.
The lawn is behind the house.
items.e: The reply explains why the lawn was not mowed: the machine did not work.

L: Is the soup homemade, or does it come out of a can?
o: The cook makes it fresh every morning.
Yes, I can come by your office tomorrow.
It comes with a small salad.
I made it home before dark.
items.e: If the cook makes it every morning, the soup is homemade.

L: Does your son still want to join the Navy when he finishes high school?
o: Now he's talking about going to college.
He joined us for dinner on Sunday.
The school is near the harbor.
items.e: The son has changed his plans: he is thinking about college instead of the Navy.

L: If my husband calls, would you tell him I'll be home by six?
o: I'll be home by six too.
He told me about it yesterday.
The six o'clock news is on.
items.e: "Pass that along" means give the message to the husband.

L: The repair shop charged us sixty dollars for parts and forty for labor.
items.q: How much did the repair cost in all?
items.e: Sixty dollars plus forty dollars makes one hundred dollars.

L: The gym opens at five in the morning on weekdays and at eight on weekends.
items.q: When does the gym open on Saturday?
items.e: Saturday is a weekend day, so the gym opens at eight.

L: The store is open from nine to nine, except on Sundays, when it closes at six.
items.q: When does the store close on Sunday?
items.e: On Sundays it closes at six.

L: Room two fourteen is on the second floor, next to the elevator.
o: On level two, right beside the elevator
On the fourteenth level, by the elevator
On the second level, beside the stairs
On the first level, across from the elevator
items.e: Room two fourteen is on the second floor, next to the elevator; fourteen is part of the room number, not the floor.

L: The parking lot holds two hundred cars, and it's already half full.
items.q: How many cars are in the lot?
items.e: Half of two hundred is one hundred.

L: Please turn in your reports by seventeen hundred hours on Friday.
items.e: 1700 hours is five o'clock in the afternoon.

L: I was born on the fifth of May, and my brother was born exactly two years later.
items.e: "Exactly two years later" means the same date, two years after.

L: My next physical is in three weeks, on the twenty-first.
items.e: The physical is on the twenty-first.

L: My watch is ten minutes fast; it says nine o'clock now.
items.e: If the watch is ten minutes fast, the real time is ten minutes earlier.

L: I've lost five pounds since I started running, and I want to lose five more.
items.q: How many pounds does she want to lose in all?
items.e: Five already lost plus five more is ten pounds.

L: The car's oil should be changed every five thousand miles.
items.q: How often should the oil be changed?
items.e: The speaker says five thousand miles.

L: The battalion commander will arrive on the morning of the fourteenth.
items.e: She says the morning of the fourteenth.

L: The pool is a hundred meters from the barracks, on the left.
items.e: It is a hundred meters away, on the left.

L: In this state you must be twenty-one to rent a car.
items.q: How old must you be to rent a car?
items.e: The minimum age is twenty-one.

L: The new copier prints sixty pages a minute, twice as fast as the old one.
items.q: How fast was the old copier?
items.e: The new one is twice as fast, so the old one printed thirty.

L: The new laptop is lighter than the old one, but its battery doesn't last as long.
items.q: What is true about the new laptop?
o: It is the same as the old one.
items.e: "Doesn't last as long" means a shorter battery life.

L: You don't need to bring your own helmet; the range will provide one.
o: A helmet will be given to you.
You need to buy a helmet.
items.e: "Don't need to" means it is not necessary.

L: I'd rather walk to the post office than wait for the shuttle.
items.e: "I'd rather walk than wait" means he prefers walking.

L: I've never seen so many people at a graduation before.
o: There were more people than usual.
He has never been to a graduation.
He did not see the graduation.
items.e: "Never seen so many" means the crowd was unusually large.

L: I'm not sure whether the dining facility is open on holidays.
o: He doesn't know if it is open.
items.e: "Not sure whether" means he does not know.

L: I couldn't have done the project without my teammates.
o: His teammates helped him a lot.
items.e: "Couldn't have done it without them" means they were essential.

L: The bigger the unit, the longer it takes to deploy.
o: Large units need more time to deploy.
All units deploy at the same speed.
items.e: "The bigger ... the longer" links size with time.

L: Corporal Lee speaks Spanish better than anyone else in the company.
items.q: What is true about Corporal Lee?
o: His Spanish is the best in the company.
items.e: "Better than anyone else" means the best.

L: This is the third time this month that the elevator has broken down.
items.e: Three breakdowns in a month is a lot.

L: I wish I had bought the tickets when they were cheaper.
o: He paid a high price or missed the cheap tickets.
items.e: "I wish I had bought" expresses regret.

L: There is no need to hurry; the train has been delayed.
items.e: A delayed train gives them more time.

L: We ran out of milk, so I'll stop at the store on the way home.
items.q: Why will he stop at the store?
o: He wants to see a friend.
The store is having a sale.
items.e: "Ran out of" means there is none left.

L: I'll lend you the money as long as you pay me back by Friday.
items.q: What is the condition for the loan?
o: She must repay it by Friday.
items.e: "As long as" introduces a condition.

L: The flight attendants won't serve meals until the plane reaches cruising altitude.
o: After the plane reaches cruising altitude
items.e: "Won't ... until" means only after that point.

L: You can either take the bus at seven or wait for the van at eight.
o: The bus at seven or the van at eight
The bus at eight or the van at seven
items.e: "Either ... or" gives two options.

L: The generator needs to be serviced every two hundred hours of use.
items.q: When should the generator be serviced?
items.e: Service is needed every two hundred hours.

L: We're short of staff this week because three people are sick.
items.q: Why is the office short of staff?
items.e: "Short of staff" means not enough people; three are sick.

L: Please fill out the leave request at least two weeks before your trip.
items.q: When should the leave request be filled out?
o: Two weeks or more before the trip
items.e: "At least two weeks before" sets the minimum time.

L: Mr. Gomez retired last year, so Ms. Hill is the new manager.
items.q: Why is Ms. Hill the manager now?
o: Mr. Gomez was promoted last year.
Mr. Gomez asked her to help him.
She has worked there since last year.
items.e: Mr. Gomez retired, so Ms. Hill replaced him.

L: The radio operator repeated the message twice to make sure it was understood.
items.q: Why did the operator say the message again?
o: So that nobody would misunderstand it
Because the radio was not working well
Because he had two different messages
To practice for his radio test
items.e: He repeated it "to make sure it was understood."

L: The training room is reserved for the officers' meeting all afternoon.
items.q: Who will use the training room this afternoon?
items.e: It is reserved for the officers' meeting.

L: You'll need the commander's signature before you can order new equipment.
items.q: What must happen before new equipment can be ordered?
o: The commander must place the order.
The old equipment must be returned.
The supply clerk must approve it.
items.e: You need the commander's signature before you can order.

L: My supervisor gave me the afternoon off because I worked late yesterday.
items.q: Why did she get the afternoon off?
o: She worked late the day before.
items.e: The time off rewards her late work.

L: The computer lab will get thirty new machines next semester.
items.q: What does the woman say about the computer lab?
o: It will be better equipped next term.
It has only thirteen computers right now.
It got thirty new machines last semester.
items.e: The lab will receive thirty new computers next semester.

L: I need to renew my security clearance before the end of the month.
items.e: She has to renew her clearance.

L: The boss wants us to cut the travel budget by ten percent.
items.e: Cutting the budget means spending less.

L: The project was finished two days ahead of schedule.
items.e: "Ahead of schedule" means early.

L: Sergeant Lopez was named Soldier of the Month for his hard work.
o: He received an award for his effort.
He was promoted to sergeant this month.
He started a hard new job.
He was named after a famous soldier.
items.e: Being named Soldier of the Month is an honor for his hard work.

L: The supply clerk counted the blankets twice to be sure.
items.q: Why did the clerk count the blankets twice?
o: To be sure of the number
items.e: She wanted to be sure.

L: Take two of these pills with water after every meal.
items.q: When should the pills be taken?
items.e: The instructions say after every meal.

L: The hospital is about a ten-minute walk from the hotel.
items.e: A ten-minute walk is about ten minutes on foot.

L: Tomorrow will be sunny but very windy, with gusts up to forty miles per hour.
items.q: What will tomorrow's weather be like?
items.e: Sunny, with strong wind.

L: The bus terminal is three blocks north of the train station.
o: Three blocks north of the station
Three blocks south of the station
items.e: It is three blocks north.

L: Snow is expected in the mountains, but the valley will only get rain.
items.e: Snow is expected in the mountains; the valley will get only rain.

L: The airport shuttle picks up passengers in front of the main entrance every twenty minutes.
items.q: How often does the shuttle come?
items.e: A shuttle every twenty minutes means three per hour.

L: If the fog doesn't lift by ten, the boats will stay in the harbor and the fishing trip will be moved to Sunday.
items.q: What could cause the fishing trip to be postponed?
items.e: The trip will be moved if the fog remains, which makes it hard to see on the water.

L: To get to the gym, go straight past the chapel and turn right at the fountain.
items.q: What should you do first on the way to the gym?
items.e: You go straight past the chapel and only then turn right at the fountain.

L: The heat wave is expected to last until the end of the week.
o: It will stay hot for the rest of the week.
The heat wave ended at the end of last week.
The heat wave will last for several weeks.
It will be cooler by the middle of the week.
items.e: The heat wave is expected to continue until the end of the week.

L: Our bags were left in Chicago, so we'll get them tomorrow.
o: They were left behind in Chicago.
items.e: The bags stayed in Chicago.

L: The pilot says we'll be landing about twenty minutes early because of a strong tailwind.
o: The pilot is in a hurry.
items.e: A tailwind pushes the plane forward.

L: The clinic is closed for lunch, so come back after one.
items.e: The clinic reopens after one.

L: The forecast says we'll get two to four inches of rain tomorrow.
items.q: What does the forecast predict for tomorrow?
o: Two to four inches of snow
Rain for two to four hours
items.e: Two to four inches of rain is a few inches; the numbers are inches, not hours.

L: The tornado warning is in effect until nine o'clock tonight.
items.q: How long does the warning last?
items.e: The warning lasts until nine tonight.

L: I returned the shirt because it was too small, and they gave me my money back.
o: Gave him a larger shirt instead
Refused to take the shirt back
Gave him a gift card for the store
items.e: "Gave me my money back" is a refund.

L: Our neighbors' dog barks all night, so we haven't been sleeping well.
items.q: Why haven't they been sleeping well?
o: The neighbors' dog barks at night.
Their baby wakes up every night.
They work the night shift now.
Their street has a lot of traffic.
items.e: The barking keeps them awake.

L: My wife and I met in college, and we've been married for ten years.
items.q: What can be concluded about the man and his wife?
o: They have known each other for years.
They are both still in college now.
They got married before starting college.
They met at work ten years ago.
items.e: They met in college and have been married for ten years, so they have known each other a long time.

L: My grandmother turned ninety last month, and the whole family came to her party.
o: Ninety guests came to a party
His grandmother moved in with them
items.e: The whole family came to his grandmother's ninetieth birthday party.

L: My wife works downtown, so she takes the train instead of driving.
items.q: Why does his wife take the train?
o: She works in the city center.
She doesn't have a driver's license.
The train is cheaper than gas.
She likes to read on the train.
items.e: Working downtown is the reason.

L: I've lived in this town for five years, but I still get lost downtown.
items.q: What is true about the speaker?
items.e: Even after five years he gets lost.

L: The electric bill was higher this month because we used the air conditioner a lot.
o: They used a lot of air conditioning.
The price of electricity went down.
items.e: Heavy air conditioner use raised the bill.

L: My children are learning to swim at the base pool this summer.
items.q: What does the man say about his children?
o: They are taking swimming lessons on base.
They are teaching younger kids to swim.
They will start lessons next summer.
They work as lifeguards at the base pool.
items.e: Learning to swim this summer means they are taking swimming lessons now.

L: The baby was born at three in the morning and weighed seven pounds.
items.e: The baby was born at three in the morning.

L: I've been trying to lose weight, so I've stopped eating desserts.
items.q: Why has the man changed his eating habits?
o: He is hoping to become a bit slimmer.
He has lost his taste for sweets.
He is trying to put on weight.
He wants to save money on food.
items.e: He gave up desserts because he is trying to lose weight, that is, to become slimmer.

L: My daughter wants a puppy, but our apartment doesn't allow pets.
items.q: Why can't she have a puppy?
o: Pets are not allowed in their apartment.
items.e: The apartment rules forbid pets.

L: I always check the price per ounce to find the best deal.
items.q: What does he do when he shops?
items.e: Price per ounce helps compare.

L: Our daughter is getting married in June, and she wants a small wedding.
items.q: What kind of wedding does she want?
items.e: She wants a small wedding.

L: The sign says the store will reopen after the holiday on Tuesday.
o: The shop is shut for a holiday.
The store is having a holiday sale.
The store is opening for the first time.
The store will close for good on Tuesday.
items.e: If the store will reopen after the holiday, it is closed during the holiday.

L: All trainees must report to the auditorium at oh seven thirty for the opening ceremony.
items.q: At what time must the trainees be in the auditorium?
o: At half past seven in the morning
At half past seven in the evening
At thirteen minutes after seven in the morning
At five thirty in the afternoon
items.e: "Oh seven thirty" is military time for 7:30 in the morning.

L: The instructor marked the essay down because it was handed in late.
items.q: Why did the essay get a lower grade?
o: It was on the wrong topic.
items.e: "Handed in late" lowered the grade.

L: Please save my seat for a minute; I want to grab some popcorn before the previews are over.
items.e: Popcorn and previews before the film suggest a movie theater.

L: The grammar test was postponed because the instructor was sick.
items.e: The instructor's illness delayed the test.

L: The computer class meets on Tuesdays and Thursdays from six to eight.
items.q: When does the computer class meet?
items.e: It meets two evenings a week.

L: The listening test has fifty questions, and the reading test has forty.
items.q: What does the woman say about the two tests?
o: The reading part has ten fewer items.
The reading test has fifty questions.
Both tests are the same length.
The listening test has fifteen questions.
items.e: There are fifty listening questions and forty reading questions, so reading has ten fewer.

L: Please put your phones on silent before the lecture begins.
items.q: What should people do before the lecture?
items.e: Phones should be on silent.

L: The final exam will cover everything we studied this semester.
items.q: What will the final exam include?
o: All the material from the semester
items.e: "Everything we studied" means all the material.

L: The bookstore will buy back used textbooks at the end of the course.
items.q: What can students do when the course is over?
o: Sell their old books to the store.
Buy used textbooks at a lower price.
Exchange their books for new ones.
Return library books without a fine.
items.e: "Buy back used textbooks" means students can sell their old books to the bookstore.

L: The education center offers free English classes to military spouses.
items.q: Who can take the free English classes?
items.e: The classes are for military spouses.

L: Students must be in their rooms by twenty-two hundred on weeknights.
items.q: What time must students be in their rooms?
items.e: 2200 is ten at night.

L: The pool is reserved for the water survival class every morning until ten.
o: Other swimmers can use it after ten.
The class meets every evening at ten.
The survival course lasts ten days.
Reservations must be made by ten.
items.e: The class has the pool until ten each morning, so others can use it after that.

L: I thought the driving test would be a breeze, but the instructor made me parallel park three times before he passed me.
items.q: What can be concluded about the man's driving test?
o: It was more difficult than he expected.
It was exactly as easy as he had expected.
He had to take it three different times.
The instructor refused to let him pass.
items.e: He expected an easy test, but he had to repeat the parking several times before he passed.

L: I paid top dollar for these boots, and they started falling apart after just two weeks in the field.
items.q: What is the man complaining about?
o: The boots cost only one dollar.
He lost his boots in the field.
The boots took two weeks to arrive.
items.e: He paid a high price, yet the boots fell apart very soon.

L: The hotel near the beach won't break the bank, and it's only a short walk from the train station.
items.q: What does the man say about the hotel?
o: It is next to a bank.
It is far from the station.
It costs too much for him.
items.e: "Won't break the bank" means it is not too expensive.

L: Once the paperwork is done, we'll be home free.
o: After the paperwork, everything will be easy.
They will go home without paying.
items.e: "Home free" means the hard part is over.

L: I'm afraid I've bitten off more than I can chew with this job.
o: He took on too much work.
He ate too much at lunch.
items.e: It means accepting more than you can handle.

L: The supply sergeant bent over backwards to get us new uniforms.
o: The sergeant tried very hard to help.
items.e: "Bend over backwards" means make a great effort.

L: My new car is a lemon; it's always in the shop.
o: His car is very new and perfect.
items.e: A "lemon" is a car with many defects.

L: My hands are shaking, and I can't eat a thing; my promotion board starts in less than an hour.
o: Hungry but too busy to eat
Bored with waiting for a meeting
items.e: Shaking hands and no appetite before an important board show that he is nervous.

L: The software update erased all our files, so we're back to square one with the training schedule.
o: They need to buy new software.
The training moved to Room One.
items.e: "Back to square one" means starting again from the beginning.

L: You've got to be kidding; the test is tomorrow?
items.e: He is surprised by the news.
